items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I remember I did a recording with Cozy Cole, myself, Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines... Cozy was the drummer. And it came out under Cozy's name.

ctx.x: I don't remember. We never paid any attention to the labels, but I know Teddy Reed used to get quite a few of those things together, and then Harry Lim used to get a lot of those -- Little dates together, because I remember I did a recording with Cozy Cole, myself, Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines, guy named Billy Taylor on bass, Joe Thomas on trumpet, and I forgot who was the -- who was the drums on that date. I forgot. Cozy was the drummer.
And it came out under Cozy's name. We did some things through for the --

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: that was my second time, second year with them... that was a great little tour there with Trummy, Barney Bigard

ctx.x: Oh sure. And then I bring a couple of little charts maybe on 'Topsy' lead sheets, you know, a small group, all they need is a little trumpet, lead sheet, piano.
That poster you have up on your wall from last year in LA that you did, Barney Bigard and Trummy Young. Talk a little about that.
Oh surely. Well that was my first time seeing Trummy since, I mean working with Trummy since I left Louie.
